limitations: No Digital Macaroni hands-on test was completed.
Noloco replaced older Starter, Pro, and Business pricing with a current Free, Build, and Enterprise structure.
A severe record-limit and sync complaint reflects an older plan and a disputed account, so it is used as a sizing warning rather than a current plan fact.

claims.statement: Noloco turns tables and connected business data into internal tools and client portals with forms, views, permissions, comments, and workflows.
Free currently includes unlimited apps and team seats, 50 client seats, 2,000 records per app, and community support.
Build is currently $79 monthly with 10 included team seats, up to 1,000 client seats, all listed data sources, 25,000 records, 3,000 workflow runs, and live chat and email support.
Build charges $6 for each extra team seat and $25 monthly for each extra 25,000-record block, up to 250,000 records before a custom plan is needed.
Fast portal and internal-tool setup, data connections, flexibility, and responsive support are repeated strengths.
Missing features, visual limits, learning effort, price, sync, and record limits appear in user feedback.

One detailed G2 reviewer reports a 50,000-row limit, Xano sync failures, a slow editor, and a refund dispute; Noloco disputes important parts and says the use case exceeded the product's supported scale.

scoreRationale.onboarding: Noloco can turn an existing table into useful screens quickly.
scoreRationale.product: It is well matched to client portals and internal operations with defined rows, roles, and actions.
scoreRationale.support: Support is widely praised, though one detailed long-term dispute shows a bad outcome when scale and sync expectations diverge.
scoreRationale.billing: The new $79 Build plan is simpler, but records and team seats still need sizing before migration.
scoreRationale.overall: Noloco is a practical tool for putting a secure working layer over business data, not a blank canvas for any kind of software.

conflictsAndUnknowns: Most reviews praise support while one detailed account describes an unresolved and costly failure.
The current pricing and record limits differ from the older plan in that complaint.
